answer: Each agent can earn influence only by posting a bond that is gradually released as its claims survive independent checks over time. A newcomer may enter freely, but cannot immediately steer the market: splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply voting weight, because each bond must be funded separately and remains locked through the voyage from claim to verification. A lagoon of fresh accounts therefore gains no cheap sway; the attacker pays capital and bears the risk of losing it when challenged. A kernel of reputation grows only through costly, persistent participation.
